subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, if cot(A/2) : cot(B/2) : cot(C/2) = 3 : 5 : 7, then show that a : b : c = 6 : 5 : 4.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.76 — SAQ chapter 13 Properties of Triangles, answer 83, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: AP 17. A ratio question run backwards: the cotangent ratio is given and the side ratio wanted. The common s/Δ cancels out of the given ratio immediately. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: the same book prints 1+1+1+1 for the 4-mark answers 58 and 59 on book p.63 and 1+2+1 for answer 61 on p.64, so both shapes used in this unit are the book's own. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q17 is the Properties of Triangles slot. Together with Q24 (LAQ) this unit holds TWO slots — one of only two units to do so, Matrices being the other.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Reduce to a ratio of (s−a)
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Each cotangent is s(s−a)/Δ, and every term carries the same s/Δ — so it cancels straight out of the ratio, leaving the brackets.
steps.memory_tip: Every cotangent carries the same s/Δ, so it cancels straight out of the ratio.
lines: Take s − a = 3k, s − b = 5k, s − c = 7k  (k ≠ 0)

recall.must_convey: That s/Δ cancels from the ratio, leaving (s−a) : (s−b) : (s−c) = 3 : 5 : 7, and a constant k is introduced.
accept: the s over delta cancels from every term leaving s minus a to s minus b to s minus c as three to five to seven
write s minus a as three k and so on
the common factor cancels out of a ratio
s by delta cancel avthundi, s minus a three k ani rasta
reduce to a ratio of the brackets

steps.why: A factor common to every term of a ratio cancels completely. Spotting that turns a cotangent question into a purely algebraic one in one line.

steps.label: Find s, then the sides
steps.margin_note: The other half. Adding the three gives 3s − 2s = s = 15k; then each side follows by subtracting from s.
steps.memory_tip: Adding the three brackets gives 3s − 2s = s = 15k; each side then follows by subtracting from s.

recall.must_convey: That adding gives s = 15k, so a = 12k, b = 10k, c = 8k, and the ratio reduces to 6 : 5 : 4.
accept: adding gives s equals fifteen k then a is twelve k b is ten k c is eight k which reduces to six five four
the three brackets add to s so s is fifteen k
the sides are twelve ten eight which is six five four
add cheste s fifteen k, sides twelve ten eight, ratio six five four
find s then each side then reduce

steps.why: 12 : 10 : 8 all share a factor of 2, so the ratio reduces. Leaving it unreduced would not match the form the question asked for.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the brackets add to s, not to 3s.

insider_note: The s/Δ cancels, so the given ratio is really (s−a) : (s−b) : (s−c). Their sum is s, not 2s, and that is what fixes s = 15k and turns 3, 5, 7 into 12, 10, 8.
